B7a-01-paramecium-binary-fission-stages

Step-by-step diagram of transverse binary fission in Paramecium in five stages from left to right: (1) a full-grown slipper-shaped Paramecium with cilia, an oral groove, a large bean-shaped macronucleus, a small round micronucleus beside it and two star-shaped contractile vacuoles; (2) the micronucleus dividing into two and the macronucleus elongating; (3) a constriction forming across the middle of the cell, with each half receiving a micronucleus and half of the macronucleus; (4) the constriction deepening; (5) two small daughter Paramecia separating. Soft pale blue cytoplasm.
B7a-02-yeast-budding-stages

Step-by-step diagram of budding in yeast in four stages from left to right: (1) a single oval yeast cell with cell wall, cytoplasm, nucleus and vacuole; (2) a small bud bulging from one side with the nucleus dividing; (3) one daughter nucleus moving into the growing bud; (4) a short branched chain of yeast cells with buds of different sizes still attached. Add a fifth small drawing of a separated daughter cell and a bud scar on the parent.
B7a-03-asexual-reproduction-types-grid

A four-panel grid of other types of asexual reproduction: (1) Rhizopus growing on bread with upright sporangiophores carrying round black sporangia, one bursting and releasing tiny spores; (2) a green Spirogyra filament with spiral chloroplasts breaking into three fragments, each growing; (3) a Planaria cut into three pieces, each regrowing into a complete flatworm with eyespots; (4) a honey bee queen laying an unfertilised egg that develops into a drone.
B7a-04-asexual-vs-sexual-reproduction

A two-column comparison diagram. Left column "Asexual reproduction": one parent plant (e.g. a yam tuber sprouting several identical shoots) with arrows to three identical offspring all in the same green colour, and "clones". Right column "Sexual reproduction": a male and a female parent (e.g. two different-coloured flowers or two goats), each producing a gamete (sperm and egg) that fuse to form a zygote, with arrows to three offspring each in slightly different colours,, "fertilisation" and "variation".
B7a-05-underground-vegetative-organs

A panel of four underground storage organs used in natural vegetative propagation. (1) Onion bulb cut lengthwise showing the flat disc stem at the base, fleshy scale leaves, dry papery outer scale leaves, terminal bud in the centre, an axillary bud, and adventitious roots. (2) Cocoyam corm with ring-like nodes, scale leaves, terminal bud at the top with leaf bases, small cormels around it, and adventitious roots. (3) Ginger rhizome growing horizontally with nodes, internodes, scale leaves, axillary buds, a terminal bud turning up into an aerial shoot, and adventitious roots. (4) Irish potato tuber showing spirally arranged eyes, each with a scale-leaf scar and buds, a terminal bud cluster, the stolon scar, and one eye sprouting a shoot.
B7a-06-aboveground-vegetative-propagation

A panel of four natural vegetative propagation methods above ground. (1) A plantain plant with its pseudostem and leaves, cut away at the base to show the underground corm (rhizome) with two suckers emerging nearby: one sword sucker with narrow leaves and one water sucker with broad leaves. (2) A pineapple plant with a fruit showing the crown on top, slips below the fruit and a sucker at the base. (3) A strawberry or Bermuda grass plant with a horizontal runner on the soil surface, roots and a new plantlet at each node. (4) A thick, notched Bryophyllum leaf lying on moist soil with several small plantlets with tiny roots growing from the notches along its margin.
B7a-07-plant-stem-cuttings

Three panels showing cuttings. (1) A cassava stem being cut with a cutlass into 20–25 cm pieces with several nodes each, and the pieces planted slanting in a ridge with buds pointing upward and two-thirds buried; one older cutting showing adventitious roots, new shoots and swelling root tubers. (2) A sugar cane sett with two nodes laid horizontally in a furrow, with shoots from the buds and roots from the nodes. (3) A hibiscus stem cutting with lower leaves removed, its base dipped in rooting powder and planted in a pot of moist soil, with new roots forming.
B7a-08-cleft-grafting-stages

Step-by-step diagram of cleft grafting in four stages: (1) a young rootstock seedling cut across with a vertical cleft split in the middle of the stump; (2) a scion shoot with buds and a wedge-shaped base; (3) the scion inserted into the cleft with the cambium layers lining up (green line highlighted on both); (4) the union tied firmly with tape and the scion covered by a small transparent polythene bag, with new leaves growing from the scion buds. Add a small inset of approach grafting with a potted rootstock bound to a branch of the parent tree.
B7a-09-t-budding-propagation

Step-by-step diagram of T-budding in five stages: (1) a rootstock stem with a T-shaped cut in its bark; (2) the bark flaps lifted; (3) a shield-shaped piece of bark with a single bud being sliced from a bud stick of the parent plant, with the leaf cut off leaving a short stalk; (4) the bud shield slid under the bark flaps with the bud pointing up; (5) the union tied with budding tape leaving the bud exposed, and a later stage with the stock cut back above the bud and a new shoot growing from it. Add a small inset of patch budding on a rubber seedling.
B7a-10-layering-propagation-methods

Two side-by-side diagrams of layering. Left: simple (ground) layering of a hibiscus or Ixora shrub, with a long low branch bent down, a small wound on its underside buried in moist soil and held down with a forked peg, the tip of the branch tied upright to a small stake, and new roots forming at the buried wound; a dotted line shows where the branch will be cut from the parent. Right: air layering (marcotting) on a guava or citrus branch, in three small stages: (a) a ring of bark removed from the branch exposing the white wood; (b) the ring wrapped in a ball of moist coconut fibre and soil covered with clear polythene tied at both ends; (c) roots visible inside the polythene and a dotted cutting line just below the ball.
